facts.statement: The genus Hudiesaurus was described by Chinese paleontologist Dong Zhiming in 1997.
facts.quote: It was described by Chinese paleontologist Dong Zhiming in 1997.

facts.statement: The genus Hudiesaurus originally contained a single species, H. sinojapanorum, based on a single vertebra.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Hudiesaurus sinojapanorum, named based on a single vertebra.

facts.statement: Fossils of Hudiesaurus were unearthed by the Sino-Japanese Silk Road Expedition near Qiketai in Shanshan, Xinjiang province, from the Kalaza Formation.
facts.quote: These fossils were unearthed by the Sino-Japanese Silk Road Expedition near Qiketai in Shanshan, Xinjiang province in rock layers coming from the Kalaza Formation.

facts.statement: Hudiesaurus lived during the Late Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages of the Late Jurassic, approximately 154 to 143 million years ago.
facts.quote: This formation dates to between the Late Kimmeridgian and Tithonian stages of the Late Jurassic, 154 to 143 million years ago.

facts.statement: Fossils of Hudiesaurus were first discovered in 1993 in the Turpan Basin near Qiketai, Xinjiang, by the Sino-Japanese Silk Road Dinosaur Expedition.
facts.quote: Fossils of Hudiesaurus were first discovered in 1993 by members of the Sino-Japanese Silk Road Dinosaur Expedition in the Turpan Basin near the town of Lanngou in Qiketai, Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region in western China.

facts.statement: The initial discovery included a presacral vertebra (IVPP V11120), an incomplete right forelimb (IVPP V11121-1), and four teeth (IVPP V11121-2) found in quarries about 1 km apart.
facts.quote: The remains found consisted of a presacral (before the sacral) vertebra, cataloged as IVPP V11120 at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing, from one quarry as well as an incomplete right forelimb (IVPP V11121-1) and four teeth (IVPP V11121-2) from a quarry about 1 km away.

facts.statement: The name Hudiesaurus means "butterfly lizard," referencing the split neural spines of the holotype vertebra.
facts.quote: The generic name Hudiesaurus derives from the Chinese Pinyin "Hudie" for butterfly, in reference to the bifurcated (split) neural spines of the vertebra, and the Latin root "sauros" meaning "lizard", a common suffix for dinosaur names.

facts.statement: Hudiesaurus is considered one of the largest dinosaurs, with estimates reaching 32 meters in length and 55 tonnes in mass.
facts.quote: Hudiesaurus is one of the largest dinosaurs known, possibly reaching 32 m in length and 55 tonne in body mass.

facts.statement: The holotype vertebra of Hudiesaurus is robust and wide, measuring 539 mm across.
facts.quote: Its vertebra is robust, large, and wide, with a width of 539 mm.

facts.statement: The bifurcated neural spine of Hudiesaurus suggests it had strong lateral control over its neck.
facts.quote: The neural spine (the uppermost part of a vertebra) is bifurcated (split at the top), indicating that Hudiesaurus had strong lateral control over its neck.

facts.statement: Large cavities called pleurocoels on the vertebrae of Hudiesaurus likely stored pneumatic air sacs.
facts.quote: On the sides of the centrum (body of the vertebra) are pleurocoels (large cavities) which would store pneumatic air sacs.

facts.statement: As a mamenchisaurid, Hudiesaurus was likely a four-legged herbivore that browsed at low to medium heights.
facts.quote: Being a mamenchisaurid, Hudiesaurus was likely a low or medium-browsing, four-legged herbivore.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding the position of the holotype vertebra, with initial identification as a dorsal vertebra later challenged by analysis suggesting it is a cervical vertebra.
facts.quote: Dong believed that the vertebra was a dorsal (trunk) vertebra, but later analysis suggested that it is one of the last cervical (neck) vertebrae.

facts.statement: In 2004, Paul Upchurch and colleagues criticized the assignment of a forelimb and teeth to Hudiesaurus due to insufficient evidence.
facts.quote: In 2004, the assignment of the forelimb and teeth to Hudiesaurus was criticized by Paul Upchurch and colleagues, who noted that there was no sufficient evidence to refer those fossils to the taxon.

facts.statement: Paleontologists Mark Hallet and Matt Wedel theorized that the bifurcated neural spines of Hudiesaurus facilitated high-browsing.
facts.quote: The bifurcated neural spines of Hudiesaurus would have allowed for more lateral control over its neck, which paleontologists Mark Hallet and Matt Wedel theorized was beneficial for high-browsing.

facts.statement: Other studies suggest that the bifurcated neural spines indicate a horizontal neck posture rather than high-browsing capabilities.
facts.quote: However, other studies have noted that this is indicative of a horizontal neck and feeding posture.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Hudiesaurus to be 25 meters long and weigh 25 tonnes in 2016.
facts.quote: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at 25 m and its weight at 25 tonne.

facts.statement: Researchers Rubén Molina-Pérez and Asier Larremendi estimated Hudiesaurus at 30.5 meters long and 44 tonnes if the vertebra is dorsal.
facts.quote: In their book Dinosaurs Facts and Figures, researchers Rubén Molina-Pérez and Asier Larremendi estimated Hudiesaurus to be 30.5 m in length with a shoulder height of 5.5 m and mass of 44 tonne if the vertebra is a dorsal vertebra.

facts.statement: Molina-Pérez and Larremendi noted that if the vertebra is cervical, Hudiesaurus would reach 32 meters in length and 55 tonnes in weight.
facts.quote: However, they noted that if the vertebra is a cervical vertebra, its length would be 32 m and its weight 55 tonne.

facts.statement: The known Hudiesaurus fossil is nearly complete, although a portion of the right diapophysis was damaged and repaired with plaster.
facts.quote: The vertebra is nearly complete, though much of the right diapophysis was damaged and restored with plaster.

facts.statement: Large air-filled cavities called pleurocoels are found on the sides of the Hudiesaurus vertebrae to help keep the bones light.
facts.quote: Large pleurocoels (openings that contained large air cavities) are present on the lateral (side) surfaces of the centrum.

facts.statement: The Hudiesaurus vertebra features divided neural spines that form a U-shaped cleft, a trait shared with its relative Mamenchisaurus.
facts.quote: The neural spines are bifurcated (divided) and form a U-shaped shallow cleft, a characteristic found in relatives like Mamenchisaurus.

facts.statement: Hudiesaurus is classified within the family Mamenchisauridae, a group of sauropods that lived in Asia and Africa during the Jurassic and Cretaceous periods.
facts.quote: Hudiesaurus belonged to the family Mamenchisauridae, a group of sauropods that existed during the Jurassic and Cretaceous in Asia and Africa.

facts.statement: Hudiesaurus was comparable in size to other mamenchisaurids like Xinjiangtitan (30-32 meters long) and Mamenchisaurus sinocanodorum (26 meters long).
facts.quote: Xinjiangtitan and Mamenchisaurus sinocanodorum were comparable in size to Hudiesaurus, being 30 - 32 m and 26 m long respectively.

facts.statement: Some researchers, such as Upchurch, have argued that Hudiesaurus should be classified as an indeterminate eusauropod rather than a specific mamenchisaurid.
facts.quote: However, Upchurch stated that Hudiesaurus was an indeterminate eusauropod.

facts.statement: Hudiesaurus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, approximately 152.21 to 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (152.21 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: Hudiesaurus fossils are found in the lower section of the Kalaza Formation within the Turpan and Junggar Basins in China.
facts.quote: Hudiesaurus is known from the lower section of the Kalaza Formation in China, one of several fossiliferous formations in the Turpan Basin and Junggar Basin.

facts.statement: The environment where Hudiesaurus lived consisted of terrestrial or river-deposited sediments, preserved in thick red sandstones and mudstones.
facts.quote: The Kalaza Formation itself is composed of thick red sandstones in mudstones deposited in terrestrial or fluvial environments.

facts.statement: The Late Jurassic habitat of Hudiesaurus was warm and seasonally dry, featuring alluvial deltas, before transitioning to more arid conditions.
facts.quote: It was warm and seasonally dry, though towards the Cretaceous it transitioned to arid or semi-arid, during the Late Jurassic, with alluvial deltas running through the area.

facts.statement: The genus Hudiesaurus was named by Dong in 1997.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Hudiesaurus (genus), Dong 1997

facts.statement: The type species for the genus Hudiesaurus is Hudiesaurus sinojapanorum.
facts.quote: Type species: Hudiesaurus sinojapanorum

facts.statement: Hudiesaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia
